goal: 以成熟開源方案縮短外文 canonical Work → 即時繁體中文閱讀層的工程，不整套搬入任何單一產品。

references.doNotCopy: Do not vendor/fork wholesale into Westside Watch; AGPL boundary and excessive product scope make selective architectural borrowing preferable.

references.license: open source; verify exact current license before vendoring
references.fit: Strong candidate for reader kernel or interface model because Dawn already uses remote-first sources.
Borrow segmentation, provider and bilingual alignment ideas; Dawn should translate lazily in-reader rather than generate a second translated ebook by default.
Cache/resume/provider design is directly useful; Calibre plugin shell is not.

references.license: project-specific open source; verify component licenses before code reuse
references.fit: Use only for PDF/document path; do not force EPUB/text through PDF pipeline.
Useful later for contextual reading assistance, but not required for first translation MVP.
Borrow UX grammar; hardware/native stacks are not Dawn dependencies.

recommendedArchitecture.readerKernel: foliate-js-style book abstraction for reflowable ebooks; existing Dawn remote reader/source adapters remain authoritative
recommendedArchitecture.pdfPath: BabelDOC/PDFMathTranslate-style extraction/layout path only when source is PDF
recommendedArchitecture.translationCore: small Dawn-owned adapter interface inspired by Koodo/Calibre plugin: translate(segment, from, zh-Hant, context, terminology)
recommendedArchitecture.segmentation: chapter → block/paragraph stable segment IDs; never translate whole book synchronously
recommendedArchitecture.cache: content-hash + source-language + target-language + translation-engine/prompt-policy version; resume partial chapters
recommendedArchitecture.remoteFirst: resolve source text/reader remotely when allowed; no mandatory download
recommendedArchitecture.terminology: Dawn-owned terminology/entity layer overrides generic provider output for names, theology, history and established bibliographic translations
recommendedArchitecture.rights: separate source Work rights, host delivery terms, transformation/cache rights and reference-edition rights
recommendedArchitecture.hardGate: Bible text / Bible translations / Hebrew-Greek Scripture are excluded before translation dispatch

existingChineseEditionReference.use: bibliographic and terminology alignment only unless explicit rights permit more
forbidden: full-text ingestion of copyrighted Chinese edition
persistent cache of protected Chinese text

mvpCuts: Do not build our own EPUB parser from zero
Do not build our own PDF layout engine from zero
Do not generate translated EPUB/PDF as the primary reading path
Do not require full-book translation before opening
Do not couple translation to one paid API
Do not mix Bible translation into this tool
Do not fork a full reader application when a rendering kernel/provider pattern is sufficient
engineeringConclusion: There is no need to invent the full product. Mature open-source projects already solve most low-level reader, segmentation, provider, cache, bilingual-layout and PDF-layout problems. Dawn's proprietary value should stay in canonical collection identity, remote-first source resolution, rights gates, terminology/entity memory, editorial layers and the seamless Chinese reading experience across the collection.
